ember-orange.$description: Ember Orange — Primary action background, accent text, highlight words in headlines, fire icon, active tab underline, badge dots, link strokes — the system's only chromatic signal

ember-glow-light.$description: Ember Glow (light) — Soft orange-tinted shadow halos behind orange buttons and badges, giving them a warm bloom without raising elevation

ember-wash-deep.$description: Ember Wash (deep) — Secondary warm-tinted shadow wash, used for outer glow rings on highlighted cards and code windows

gridline.$description: Gridline — Dominant hairline border, card outlines, input strokes, code window dividers, grid background lines — the structural skeleton of every screen

ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, heading fills, icon strokes, button text on light surfaces, code text

vellum.$description: Vellum — Page and card background, the softest surface in the stack; inset shadow fields use a vellum-tinted ring to create depth without darkening

slate.$description: Slate — Secondary text, muted body copy, placeholder labels, disabled-state copy

graphite.$description: Graphite — Link text in body copy, supporting paragraphs, slightly lighter than Ink for inline emphasis

ash.$description: Ash — Tertiary text, helper text, subtle icon strokes, caption-tier metadata

stone.$description: Stone — Placeholder text in inputs and code blocks, very light body text where contrast is deliberately reduced

mist.$description: Mist — Decorative strokes, faint dividers, background-pattern dots and crosses

pebble.$description: Pebble — Muted button text on neutral surfaces, subtle UI labels

suisse.$description: Primary interface and headline face. The 450 weight (a custom intermediate between regular and medium) is distinctive — it gives body text a slightly denser feel than a standard 400, and headings carry weight 500 for calm authority rather than boldness. Tracking tightens at display sizes (-0.01em at 60px, -0.005em at 40-52px) and opens slightly (+0.01-0.02em) at caption sizes for legibility.

geist-mono.$description: Code, technical labels, and any developer-facing micro-copy. Used for code blocks, tab labels in code-switcher UI, URL examples, and inline code snippets. Geist Mono's clean monospace geometry pairs with Suisse's humanist proportions without visual conflict.
